title: Dedicated Fleet Burst Slate & SLO Ticker — compact dashboard prototype
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, operational dashboard surface for Dedicated GPU fleets that combines a burst policy composer with a lightweight SLO ticker and cost-meter. The goal is to let platform engineers and SREs quickly: 1) see fleet health at-a-glance, 2) author and preview burst/autoscaling policies, 3) understand cost impact and SLO risk before applying changes, and 4) trigger safe rollouts with built-in fallback presets. Deliverables: Figma prototype (desktop & narrow tablet), annotated handoff spec, micro-interaction tokens for policy preview, accessibility checklist, and a short demo video for PM/Eng review. Constraints: must fit existing Console grid, reuse existing Redwood color tokens and charting components, operate without additional backend endpoints (use preview simulation mode), and show conservative cost estimates (upper-bound). Success metrics: reduce time-to-configure burst policy by 40% (measured in sessions), reduce rollback incidents in canary rollouts by 25%, and increase confidence score in UX research from 3.2 to 4.1 (5-point scale).
comments: 2025-11-05 Asha Kapoor: Kickoff — scoped MLP for burst composer + SLO ticker. Decided to prioritize a preview simulation instead of requiring infra changes for initial rollout. Assigned Riley to run prototype iterations.

2025-11-08 Riley Chen: Low-fi wireframes completed. Two layout directions: Compact Tile (single-row quick controls) vs. Expanded Composer (three-column authoring flow). Shared frames in Figma. Linked to artifact.

2025-11-10 PM feedback (Miguel Santos): Prefer Compact Tile as default for operators with quick expand to full composer. Need explicit cost delta line and an obvious 'safety reserve' knob to prevent burst from exhausting reserved capacity.

2025-11-11 Eng review (Anika Patel): Backend requirements flagged for live previews. For MLP we'll surface a simulated 'preflight estimate' using historical usage percentiles. ENG-20456 owner to mock an API endpoint for simulation responses.

2025-11-12 Design review (Riley): Updated prototype to include SLO Ticker (current error budget, 24h SLA drift, projected breach time) and a Burst Credit Bank visualization (consumable bar with recharge rate). Added 'Risk Mode' toggle (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive).

2025-11-14 Research (Nora Li): 6 usability sessions with infra engineers. Findings: users liked the immediate cost delta but wanted clearer mapping from policy knobs to expected latency impact. Added a small 'Latency Impact' sparkline to composer preview.
2025-11-15 PM sign-off (Miguel Santos): OK to move to In Review. Request to add keyboard shortcuts and ARIA labels for key controls. Rafael (Eng) to confirm accessibility constraints.

2025-11-17 Eng feedback (Rafael Gomez): Minor layout changes to allow for longer pool names; suggested truncation rules. Confirmed simulation API contract and added ENG-20789 to provide test data. Noted a follow-up to add server-side validation for policy ranges.

2025-11-18 Riley Chen: Updated final frames and generated handoff tokens. Prepared acceptance criteria and QA checklist. Pushed PR for design tokens and micro-interaction specs. Ready for stakeholder review this week.
